steps.title: Declare the parameters
notes: Fill contours are off by default. Switched on, there are two rings, 0.1 mm apart. Unlike the following borders, alternate_per_contour is on: neighbouring fill rings run in opposite directions.
The count goes up to 50: enough rings to fill a thin region completely, without any hatch.

lines: // Off by default. Extra concentric rings inside the borders (default 2,
// 0.1 mm apart), between the borders and the hatch.

steps.title: Read the values from the profile
notes: The group becomes part.fill_contour, with the same fields as the following borders. That is why one function can create both.

steps.title: The rings continue inside the borders
notes: compute_insets starts the fill contours at the innermost ring so far: the first border at 0.06 mm when the following borders are off. Five rings land at 0.16, 0.26, 0.36, 0.46 and 0.56 mm.
The hatch moves with them: 0.56 + 0.05 = 0.61 mm. Everything narrower than 1.22 mm gets rings only.

lines: // Fill contours continue inside the innermost border.

steps.title: Thin regions: rings instead of hatch
notes: In the 1 mm tab, half the width is 0.5 mm. The rings at 0.16 to 0.46 mm still fit, the one at 0.56 mm and the hatch at 0.61 mm do not: the offset of the island is empty there.
That matches the Exposure Preview: the hatch now ends at x = 17.68 mm and the tab, which starts at x = 18 mm, is filled with orange rings only.

lines: function process_contour_rings(a_ctx, a_island, a_result, a_cfg, a_insets, a_bsid, a_bsid_ds, a_split, a_isl_info)
let l_split_info = { islid: a_isl_info.islid, bounds: a_isl_info.bounds, ds: a_isl_info.ds, split: a_split };
// The ring is empty if the island is too small for this inset;
emit_contour(a_ctx, a_result, l_res.hatch, a_cfg, i, a_bsid, a_bsid_ds, l_split_info);

steps.title: The hatch area shrinks
notes: process_part_hatches offsets the island by the hatch inset. Every extra ring shrinks that area all around; if it becomes empty, there is no hatch at all, as in the section through the tab.

lines: function process_part_hatches(a_ctx, a_island, a_result, a_insets, a_isl_info, a_us)
// Area inside the innermost contour ring (plus hatch offset).

steps.title: Laser settings and order
notes: Fill contours (BSID 300) run at 200 W and 1000 mm/s, closer to the hatch than to the borders. Scan order 60 exposes them right after the hatches and before the borders.

recipes.title: Fill contours on by default
recipes.why: Your parts have many thin ribs that should be filled with rings.
recipes.result: New profiles start with two fill rings at 0.16 and 0.26 mm; the hatch then starts at 0.31 mm.

recipes.title: More rings by default
recipes.why: Ribs up to about 1.2 mm should be filled with rings only.
recipes.result: Five rings, as in the video. Set Fill contours to 5 in Try it and look at the tab.

recipes.title: Closer fill rings
recipes.why: A ring spacing of 0.1 mm leaves only 20 µm overlap with a 0.12 mm track.
recipes.result: The fill rings are 0.08 mm apart (the first stays 0.1 mm inside the border). Compare the overlap in the Section view.

recipes.title: Faster fill contours
recipes.why: Fill contours inside the part do not form the surface; they can use hatch-like settings.
recipes.result: Fill contour default 240 W at 1200 mm/s. For one profile, change Scanning › Fill contour in the dialog instead.
